tldr: A check's description now has a limit of 10,000 characters. The API, the dashboard form and the edit dialog all enforce it, and the dashboard returns 400 on invalid input.
intent: Keep check descriptions to a bounded size on every path that writes them.

story.heading: API now limits desc to 10,000 characters
story.body: The Spec model of the management API rejects a longer desc on create and update.

story.heading: Dashboard form applies the same limit
story.body: NameTagsForm gets max_length=10000 on desc. The edit dialog textarea stops at 10,000 characters.

story.heading: update_name now returns 400 on invalid input
story.body: Before, an invalid form skipped the save and redirected as if it worked. Now the view stops with 400.

story.heading: No change to the Check model
story.body: Check.desc keeps its type. The limit lives at the 2 entry points, so the change needs no migration.

changes.summary: The Spec model limits desc to 10,000 characters on create and update.
NameTagsForm limits desc to 10,000 characters; update_name returns 400 when the form is invalid.
The description textarea has maxlength=10000; the API docs list the new limit.

decisions.title: Validate at the entry points, not in the model
decisions.why: The API Spec and the dashboard form each check the limit. Check.desc stays as it is, so no migration runs on a large table.
decisions.alternative: A max_length on Check.desc with a migration.

decisions.title: Answer invalid dashboard input with 400
decisions.why: update_name used to skip a failed form without a sign. A 400 makes the failure visible to the caller.
decisions.alternative: Show the form error inside the dialog.
